newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says no hand in KL ban on Timor activist.
newsitem.headline: Manila says no hand in KL ban on Timor activist.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos said on Thursday he did not put pressure on Malaysia to bar a Filipino human rights activist from attending a conference on East Timor in Kuala Lumpur.
"We have nothing to do with that," Ramos told reporters.
"The Malaysian government has (its) own rules, policies and laws. I suppose they acted in accordance with their laws," he added.

Renato Constantino Jr was stopped by immigration officials at Kuala Lumpur airport on Wednesday night and barred from entering the country. He was scheduled to speak at the conference to be held in Kuala Lumpur from November 9-12.
He had organised the first such conference in Manila in 1994.
Malaysia opposes the conference for fear of harming its ties with Indonesia, which invaded East Timor in December 1975 and annexed the Portuguese colony the next year.
The United Nations still recognises Lisbon as the administering authority for the territory.
Some 200 people from 24 countries and 75 organisations plan to attend the meeting at a Kuala Lumpur hotel, organisers said.
The Philippines has banned East Timorese activist and Nobel peace laureate Jose Ramos-Horta from visiting Manila during this month's summit of the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation forum.
